subject: Request: detailed telemetry + prompt/response census for Dedicated proposal
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@ablaze.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing data for upcoming pilot

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and the autoscale behavior. We're moving fast on procurement and want to make sure the Dedicated proposal matches our real traffic. 

Can you share the checklist or census you use for traffic telemetry? Specifically we can provide a sample telemetry dump from our staging cluster (in CSV) and want guidance on what prompt/response length buckets, concurrency targets, and burst tolerances you need to size a reserved fleet.

Attaching a small telemetry sample and our SLA doc (see attachment stubs). Happy to walk through it — Elena + procurement will be on the call Thursday if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform
Ablaze.ai

Attachments: ablaze_telemetry_sample.csv (csv, 220KB), ablaze_sla_requirements.pdf (pdf, 480KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@ablaze.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing data for upcoming pilot

Marissa, Diego — forwarding Ablaze's sample. They want a clear checklist so procurement can sign a monthly commitment for Dedicated. Can we pull together a short telemetry census template that asks for:

- Prompt/response length distribution (percent in each bucket: <16, 16-64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024)
- Average tokens per call and P50/P90/P99 response length
- Concurrent session expectations (typical, peak sustained, short bursts)
- Session lifetime / KV-cache reuse rate (pct of requests that reuse context)
- Expected qps by region and daypart (UTC or local)
- Peak burst duration and frequency (e.g., 180s bursts, 10x baseline, daily/weekly)
- Failure tolerance / allowed fallback model (if dedicated unavailable, fallback to hosted?)
- Any eval prompts that are latency-sensitive (examples)
- Security/compliance must-haves (VPC, log retention)

I'll draft a one-page census and a mapping table showing how each bucket maps to GPU SKU and estimated rack-days. Diego, can you add any telemetry fields we usually need for cost modelling (e.g., tokenization overhead, batching potential)?

Elena — can we confirm you'll deliver one 24h sample CSV and one 7-day aggregate? That will let us produce a conservative sizing + a lean scenario.

Cheers,
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing data for upcoming pilot

Adding a few telemetry items to Grace's list — these materially affect batching and kernel selection: 

- Tokenization pre/post ratios (avg tokens produced vs input tokens)
- Distribution of request sequence lengths (not just response) to estimate KV cache pressure
- Percent of requests using function/tool-calls or streaming (streaming reduces batching window)
- Percent of requests that are synthetic/test traffic (we filter these)
- Typical model family (Llama2/Redwood-UL2/…); and whether they plan to change model mid-contract
- Preferred quantization profile (int8/q4/float16) if known

I'll assemble the one-pager and a quick mapping: buckets -> recommended GPU (A100 80GB / H100 / 4090 mix) -> projected tokens/hour -> conservative rack-days/month. Marissa, can you prepare the XLS mapping so we can show Ablaze 3 commitment tiers (lean / expected / growth)?

— Diego
Lead Pre-Sales Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@ablaze.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@ablaze.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing data for upcoming pilot

Grace — thanks, that list looks great. We're attaching the 24-hour sample CSV and a short README that explains the columns (timestamp, request_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, model, region, is_stream). A few clarifications inline: 

> Prompt/response length distribution
- We provide both raw prompt_tokens and response_tokens; our bias is short prompts + long generative responses (40% of responses > 512 tokens)

> Concurrent session expectations
- Baseline concurrency ~120 sessions, typical peak sustained ~600 for 10–15 minutes during business hours; rare spikes to ~3500 for ~45 seconds (launch events)

> KV-cache reuse
- ~62% of requests reuse context within a session (chat-style). Average session lifetime ~8 minutes.

> Streaming
- ~12% of requests use streaming (partial tokens delivered); these are mostly customer-facing demos and are latency-sensitive.

We should be available for a 30-minute sizing walkthrough Thursday 9:00 PT. If you want the 7-day aggregates instead, let me know and procurement can drop them in Drive.

Regards,
Elena Park
Head of Platform, Ablaze.ai

Attachment stubs: ablaze_telemetry_sample.csv, ablaze_sla_requirements.pdf
